diagnosis.reason: A global inspection found component stock for hair, cosmetics and individual garments but only thin whole-presentation labels, including occupational and age metaphors. The original top8 exposes private-room action, portrait framing, mouth expression, face occlusion, ordinary clothing/posture, a catching action and environmental portrait context. The thin corporate/elegant entries sit below top8. Thus existing meanings are poorly exposed AND the visually grounded cross-component meaning is missing; ranking alone cannot repair that content gap.

method.population: 18180 positive CIDs / 18182 RID documents; full-pool document inspection, without slot-tag prefilter
method.full_source: Checked BodyReader at installed H-F2 generation; normalized native with installed photo_canonical_source.native, read canonical conditions/effects, and compared 11 selected records with working V3 content. Exact records retained in inspected-source-records.json.
method.inventory_result: All installed record effect properties inspected: zero presentation.* / appearance.presentation anchors. This is supporting structural evidence, not by itself proof of absent semantics. Semantic inspection found thin presence labels plus richer isolated garment/makeup and adjacent photographic contracts.

confusion_boundaries: Presentation is an observable combination of grooming and attire on the same wearer. A hairstyle, lip color, suit construction or necklace in isolation remains a neighboring component role.
Portrait framing, camera height, face/garment readability and environmental cues concern capture or composition; they do not establish how the wearer has been styled.
Business-like dress cannot prove actual profession, competence, salary, personality, gender identity or social status. Adult prerequisites come from the fixed request, not dress-based age inference.

Curled, coiled, textured, short or gathered hair can each be deliberately arranged. Smooth/straight hair, makeup, a suit, a luxury brand and thin/young anatomy are not universal requirements for care or refinement.

A cosmetic-to-textile accent has appearance AND color effects; the other records impose hair/garment arrangements only. None changes gaze, expression, pose, setting, framing, lighting or a body attribute.
The loose and creased alternative denotes a visible configuration, not hygiene, poverty, laziness, mental state or verifiable past wear.
All records remain discovery-only until independent semantic/native review. Empty invented proof fields, automatic role approval and source-URL authority laundering are excluded.

sources.title: Session One Studios — Portrait Style Guide
sources.supports: First-party portrait practice treats wardrobe, grooming and preparation together; discusses garment fit, texture, hair preparation and steaming or ironing. These are practices, not universal dress standards.

sources.title: V&A — About the Fashioning Masculinities exhibition
sources.supports: Institutional fashion analysis presents diverse attire and appearance across historical and contemporary looks, explicitly including tailoring, grooming objects and conventions that change. It supports resisting a single gendered or occupational definition of refinement.

sources.title: Nikon / Antonio Martez — Face Value: A Different Take on the Beauty Portrait
sources.supports: A photographer describes coordinated fabric, makeup and lighting choices in a beauty project. Supports cross-component styling as an authored photographic practice; the proposed options do not inherit the project's cultural narrative, framing or lighting.

recommendations: Integrate the five reviewed additions as cross-component appearance meaning; retain all declared hair/garment and color effects. Do not attach role eligibility from tags or new prose alone.
Run the exact original query unchanged against the complete rebuilt pool. Assess useful meaning and adjacency; do not merely count lexical overlap or train the ranker against this probe.
Audit the corporate professional and mature elegant labels separately for occupational/age metaphors. Their current content cannot be treated as complete visual specifications.
Check three additional independent intents below, including casual and loose alternatives, to test meaning coverage rather than just refinement retrieval.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Develop a carefully attended everyday appearance using soft clothing and arranged textured hair.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: The existing adult wears casual separates; keep their expression, body shape and setting fixed.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Link the subject's grooming, applied cosmetics and one fabric accessory into an expressive but coherent personal look.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: An adult fashion portrait; color relationships can change, while profession and personality remain undeclared.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Give the adult a visibly loose, lived-in arrangement through hair separation and irregular garment finishing.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: Preserve facial expression and body pose; describe the visible styling without judgments about the person.
